summary:
Auditor A. No blocking defect found. I could not show that the corrected adapters are inexact or carry information beyond the published instances; I could show that the kernel's layout check is incomplete in one respect that none of the seven environments triggers.

What holds, with my own parsers and evaluators (no rsi6 code in them):
- Knapsack: all 180 problems (30 per class, 6 classes) x 2 seeds. var_attr is (n, 31): column 0 the profit, columns 1..m the instance's coefficients under a seeded permutation of items and of constraints, columns m+1..30 exactly +0.0. partial_totals, the start/candidates/assign/totals path (through the view and on the adapter's object), evaluate, decode and Environment.score agree exactly with my evaluator on 6480 complete selections (3676 feasible, 2804 infeasible) and 9000 partially decided states. 0 failures. The name-to-problem mapping is confirmed independently: the LP optimum of my parse equals the LP optimum published under the same name for 180 of 180 (largest relative difference 4.5e-11; 0 of 180 against the neighbouring name).
- Regression: all 118 used laws x 2 seeds. Presented inputs are the published input columns in a seeded permuted order followed by exactly-zero columns, bit for bit; observed targets and the scorer's target are the published value columns; no query equals an observed row; the training flag changes only the attached target. 0 failures.
- Information: the public fields of the view hold only the instance's numbers; limits, best values, names and classes are in no array; changing the limits changes no field. Zero columns are always last and reveal only m or d (plus the benchmark maximum, 30 and 8).
- Layout: one kernel layout and one learner descriptor list per environment over 3196 constructed problems (7 environments, training and fresh, 7 seeds, 9 versions).
- Claims: learner.py, version.py and problem.py have the recorded hashes; the diff is the whole change to its four files (git blob hashes match in both directions); 38 recorded runs of the five recorded environments repeat identically under the corrected kernel; the ledger chain is intact (1211 records, no run on knapsack or regression); the registration digest is unchanged.

Findings: 1 major (run.layout() does not record capacity.max() > 1, which the learner's Layout reads; on fixtures the kernel accepts such a mix and the learner either fails inside acquire or, for index-ordered problems, silently cuts the weight vector by position), 3 minor (the learner part of the third new test performs zero learning rounds; 'one to nine input variables' is wrong, the data have one to eight; 'before the learner is called' is not true for a deviating fresh problem), and notes.

Rules kept: the learner was never called on a knapsack or regression instance (only on recorded runs of the other five environments via measure() without any ledger write, and on made-up fixtures). No network (subprocess guarded). Nothing under REPO was written (no file newer than the diff, no __pycache__). All scripts and their outputs are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-rsi-metaforge-core/49317f35-39aa-5636-a36c-c80f42cd346e/scratchpad/audit2/work_a (a*.py, a*.out). Every script was run as: cd /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-rsi-metaforge-core/49317f35-39aa-5636-a36c-c80f42cd346e/scratchpad/audit2/repo && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 python3 -B <script>.

findings.what: The check is incomplete: the learner's Layout also depends on whether options can be reused (learner.py line 93: reusable = capacity is None or capacity.max() > 1, which switches the descriptors 'usage' and 'optsum[..]'), and layout() records only 'capacity is None'. Two instances of one environment whose capacities differ across that line have the same kernel layout and different descriptor lists. The kernel then accepts the environment. For problems in free order the learner fails inside acquire, as in the original event. For problems assigned in index order nothing fails and the weight vector of the first problem is cut by position on the others, so a weight reaches another descriptor. No environment in REGISTRY is affected (reusable is uniform in all five assignment environments), so round 2 is not at risk; the target adapters are still to be written and will rely on this check, and the new test compares run.layout() only.
findings.evidence: work_a/a41_layout_gap.py (made-up fixtures, 6 variables, 8 options; first training instance holds 2 per option, the others 1) printed: 'ordered=True: run.layout equal: True ... descriptors, options hold 2: [opt:dsoft, opt:usage, opt:vo[0]]; options hold 1: [opt:dsoft, opt:vo[0]]'; 'run.measure, ordered=True: ACCEPTED, no error ... constructions in which the parameter vector was longer than the problem's own descriptor list: 1058 of 1602; (descriptors, parameters) = [(2, 3)]'; 'run.measure, ordered=False: the kernel did not refuse; the learner failed: ValueError: matmul ... (size 4 is different from 3), raised in: learner.py:construct <- learner.py:_rollouts <- learner.py:_acquire_assign'; and for one such fixture 'total with the vector cut by position 0.5579 (the usage weight acts on vo[0]), with the weights taken by name 2.3875'. work_a/a40_layout.py printed reusable per environment: jobshop {True: 392}, binpacking {True: 308}, quadassign {False: 392}, pmedian {True: 210}, knapsack {True: 392}.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the element 'P.capacity is None or int(P.capacity.max()) > 1' to layout(), and let test_layout_is_the_same_for_every_instance also compare Layout(view(P), versions.default()).names for assignment environments, so the test follows whatever the learner reads. This changes the hash of run.py in corrections.json; it changes no recorded result, since all seven environments are uniform in that element.

findings.where: rsi6/tests/test_kernel.py, test_padded_columns_are_exact_and_learnable; rsi6/registry/corrections.json 'what'[3] ('zero columns are exact and can be learned from, on made-up numbers')
findings.what: The part of the test that calls the learner does not exercise learning. With the test's budget (20 times the construction units) acquire performs no round and no construction, so the code path in which the registered run stopped (construct inside _rollouts) is never reached. 'The learner learns from them' is not established by the test, and with the same budget the uncorrected presentation passes that part too; only the test's first assert (one layout, shape (14, 6)) separates the two. The correction itself works: with the registered factor 40 the padded problems are learned from and the unpadded ones raise the original error.
findings.evidence: work_a/a42_tests.py printed: 'PASS test_padded_columns_are_exact_and_learnable (learner calls inside: acquire 1, apply 1)' and, for the same numbers, 'iterations 0 | constructions 0 | learned False | failed: decide: the budget did not allow one round of learning'. work_a/a43_third_test.py printed: 'zero columns, budget factor 20: iterations 0, constructions 0, learned False'; 'zero columns, factor 40: iterations 1, constructions 64, learned True, failed: None'; 'zero columns, factor 200: iterations 6, constructions 384, learned True'; 'no zero columns, factor 20: layouts 3; acquire returned: iterations 0 ...'; 'no zero columns, factor 40: acquire RAISED ValueError: matmul ...'.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a factor of at least 40.0 in the test and assert report['iterations'] >= 1 and report['failed'] is None; or reword the test and the record to what is asserted (one layout, exact evaluation, a well-formed answer).

findings.where: rsi6/kernel/run.py, measure() / scores(); rsi6/registry/corrections.json 'what'[2] ('refuses an environment whose training or fresh problems differ in generic layout, before the learner is called')
findings.what: True for training problems only. Fresh problems are built and checked one at a time inside scores(), after learner.acquire has run and after learner.apply has answered the fresh problems before the deviating one. The run is then lost by an exception (nothing is recorded), but the learner has been called on the environment.
findings.evidence: work_a/a41_layout_gap.py, part 3 (prediction fixture, four uniform training problems, the fourth fresh problem with one more column) printed: 'refused with: late-uneven-fixture: instances of one environment must have the same generic layout' and 'calls of the learner before the refusal: acquire 1, apply 3'. For uneven training problems work_a/a42_tests.py counted 'acquire 0, apply 0'.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute the layouts of the fresh problems (and of the training problems rebuilt for scoring) before learner.acquire; construction is cheap and uses no meter. Or reword to 'before the learner is called on that problem'.

findings.where: rsi6/learner/learner.py _rank (frozen, not in the diff) together with the zero columns of rsi6/environments/knapsack.py
findings.what: Zero columns are inert for the learner under feat.scale minmax and z, but not under rank: _rank turns a constant column into a ramp over the index, so each zero column becomes the item's position (after relabelling: noise) in the variable descriptors va[c], and [-1, +1] for [left, taken] in optsum[c]. On a 5-constraint problem these 25 descriptors would be weighted by weights that mean real constraints on 30-constraint problems. It is latent in this experiment: generation 0 and every nominee in the ledger use minmax, so no version that can run in the gate, the confirmation or the target test uses rank.
findings.evidence: work_a/a41_layout_gap.py, part 4 printed: '_mm(zeros): [0.0, ...] | _zc(zeros): [0.0, ...] | _rank(zeros): [-1.0, -0.6, -0.2, 0.2, 0.6, 1.0]', '_rank(zeros(2)): [-1.0, 1.0]', 'knapsack 5.100-00, feat.scale=minmax: ... non-zero entries 0 of 2500', 'feat.scale=z: ... 0 of 2500', 'feat.scale=rank: min -1.000 max +1.000 non-zero entries 2500 of 2500; all 25 columns identical: True'. work_a/a01_ledger.py printed: 'nominee versions with feat.scale: {464ea7440b21: minmax, cd349a06ef6d: minmax, 3a5b3ee1350b: minmax, b108b1ce6514: minmax}'.
findings.suggested_fix: No code change (the learner is frozen). State in the record that the padding is exact for the problem and inert for the learner under minmax and z only.

findings.where: rsi6/kernel/run.py layout(), prediction branch; rsi6/kernel/problem.py PredictProblem.__init__ (frozen, not in the diff)
findings.what: The fourth element of the prediction layout (qry_x.shape[1]) can never differ from the third: the constructor reshapes the queries to the observed entities' number of columns. An adapter that gave queries with another number of columns is therefore not refused by layout(); the queries are silently re-cut (or the constructor raises when the sizes do not divide).
findings.evidence: work_a/a41_layout_gap.py, part 2 printed: 'observed entities with 4 columns, 12 queries with 3 columns -> qry_x.shape (9, 4) | run.layout (predict, False, 4, 4)'.

findings.what: Three small points of the record. (a) 'files' pins six files but not rsi6/tests/test_kernel.py, the fourth file of the diff (its SHA-256 in REPO is f4adeab51f33ecea5ea6d23bc02c1277704a8569fba81f0306a53585bd7dcdf5); in the audit copy that file and corrections.json carry a later time (13:41:06) than the record's utc (13:38:32Z). (b) 'independent_audit' is null. (c) 'stopped with an error at the first run of the learner on the environment knapsack' is shorter than what the code does: the gate hands 12 jobs (6 knapsack, 6 regression) to a pool of 4 workers and Pool.map raises only when all have ended, so measure() was also entered for regression in that attempt. This is an inference from the code, not an observation. It does not touch 'scores_seen_before_the_choice: none': in both environments acquire raises before any fresh problem is answered, and the ledger holds no record of either.

findings.where: rsi6/learner/learner.py _describe (frozen, not in the diff) on the data of rsi6/environments/regression.py
findings.what: Outside the diff and not caused by the padding, but it will shape the regression numbers of round 2. The files hold physical magnitudes down to 1e-38, and the learner's test for a constant is absolute (std < 1e-12, then scale 1.0). 5 of the 24 fresh laws have observed targets under that test (1 in the gate half, 4 in the confirmation half; 0 of the 16 training laws). On such a law the untrained answer is unaffected, while an accepted fitted predictor answers at the wrong magnitude and scores 0. 8 of the 24 fresh laws and 4 of the 16 training laws also have a real input column under the test, which the learner then treats exactly like a zero column. The rule of freeze_L0.json forbids changing this to raise a score; the result should be read with it, and the two halves are hit unequally.

findings.where: rsi6/data/regression/medium/*/feynman-iii.17.37.txt as used by rsi6/environments/regression.py (not in the diff)
findings.what: A third degenerate law besides the two that are refused: its published value equals its first published input bit for bit in 122 of the 128 queries (and 250 of the 256 observed rows), because 1 + alpha*cos(theta) rounds to 1. For this law the hidden target is therefore present in the presented inputs. It is published data, not something the adapter adds, and the law is in neither the training nor the fresh set of split(16, 24), so no registered run uses it.

findings.suggested_fix: Nothing for round 2. If the instance set is ever revised, this law belongs with the two refused ones.
